items.statement: Promoter pledged less than 5% of personal shares to MCX for hedging; no shares pledged to banks for fund raising.
items.quote: A small percentage of my personal shareholding has been given to MCX, which is less than 5%, which is less than 5%.

items.statement: In the current quarter, promoters sold a small number of shares to raise personal money; the 5% drop in December was due to pledged shares being wrongly reported as sold.
items.quote: In this current quarter, there has been a small sale of shares from the promoters to raise a little personal money for some of the promoters. But in the December quarter, the main 5% which is there is a pledge, not a sale.

items.statement: Company is looking at a fundraise of roughly 150 crores in FY27; modalities not yet finalized.
items.quote: We are looking at a fundraise. We are still not, come up with a final proposal, but we are looking at a fundraise of roughly about 150 crores.

items.statement: Fundraise expected to be completed in the current financial year (FY27).
items.quote: We hope to do it in this financial year, definitely.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance stood at INR 707 million at end of FY26
items.quote: Cash and bank balance stood at INR 707 million.

items.statement: Inventory increased to INR 4,446 million in line with planned scale-up for upcoming season
items.quote: Inventory increased to INR 4,446 million, in line with our planned scaled up for the upcoming season, reflecting our confidence in FY27 demand.

items.statement: Finance costs increased to INR 133 million from INR 96 million reflecting deliberate working capital investment for inventory build
items.quote: Finance costs increased to INR 133 million from INR 96 million in FY25, reflecting our deliberate working capital investment to fuel the inventory build for FY27.

items.statement: Negative cash flow of about INR 13 crores due to formula effect; over INR 70 crores bank deposits lying at year end
items.quote: However, as per the formula, it is definitely going negative by about INR 13 crores, which is not a very big issue because we have almost about INR 70 crores of almost bank deposits lying up.

items.statement: Stock build-up higher this year due to good cotton production; inventory expected to liquidate over next two years
items.quote: But this year, the stock build-up has been a little more than earlier year for the simple reason because we were expecting the production of cotton to stabilize.

items.statement: Trade receivables declined from INR 48 crores to INR 28 crores due to reduced institutional sales in Q4
items.quote: You see, our outstanding are mostly towards institution. And you must have seen in the Q4, we have reduced our institutional sales as per our projections given to you. So, this is why the outstandings have declined.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improves as e-commerce model eliminates distributor and school credit, with parents paying directly on the platform.
items.quote: So, here the credit time has automatically vanished. So, we no longer have to supply to distributor, distributor to school, then school to parent, and then release the payments. Now, straightaway, parent is making to the publisher, to me directly, to the e-commerce platform.

items.statement: Inventory remains high at year-end because stock must be ready by September for October orders, but e-commerce reduces inventory cycle for those schools.
items.quote: Because, let's say, that school is somewhere in Kolkata. So, I need that, transport the product to middleman, and that particular school must be using multiple publishers. All of them will take their own sweet time to deliver that product in that school. So, stock has to be ready by September end or October first week. So, closing stock is going to be like this. It will be high.

items.statement: Company holds over INR 20 crores cash and cash equivalents, is practically debt-free with finance cost reduced to INR 35 lakhs from INR 1.18 crores.
items.quote: As can we know in our company balance sheet we had more than INR20 crores cash and cash equivalent in hand.

items.statement: Management may consider raising equity in Q4 FY26 or Q1/Q2 FY27 once leverage crosses 5x-6x range.
items.quote: Therefore, once our leverage crosses the 5x–6x range, we will certainly look at raising additional equity. In my view, if this year progresses well and things remain on track, we may consider raising equity in the fourth quarter. Otherwise, we would look to raise equity in the first or second quarter of the following year.

items.statement: Management says no external fundraise is expected because debt-to-equity is super low.
items.quote: This is not something which is, you know, we are focusing on at this point in time, because I think, you know, our debt to equi ty is super low. So we aren't, you know, really expecting any kind of external

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow post working capital changes was about INR600 crores, ~76% of EBITDA
items.quote: whatever EBITDA we generated, almost about 76% was operating cash flow post working capital change was created in that to -- in north of about INR600 crores

items.statement: FY27 target is to reach four-figure operating cash flow by recovering government and project receivables
items.quote: the idea in the current fiscal FY '27 is to take this amount to 4 figures by recovering the old government receivables and project receivables

items.statement: INR80 crores of government project receivables reduced in Q4 FY26 and INR30 crores received in April
items.quote: some INR80 crores were reduced in January to March from the government project receivables. And again, in April, we also received INR30 crores

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced by about 15 days across businesses despite market volatility
items.quote: working capital cycle has been reduced by almost about -- by 15 days in total across different businesses despite all the volatility

items.statement: Standalone FY26 net cash from operations post working capital changes was about INR350 crores; FY27 target INR750-800 crores
items.quote: we generated net cash from operations about INR350 crores post working capital change. And part of was the increase in the receivables, etc., the fact that we would expect to cover these receivables, in fact, should go down about INR450 crores from the government. With all that calculation, we are expecting the INR350 crores to grow to almost about INR750 crores, INR800 crores is our anticipation

items.statement: Expect INR150 crores of government benefits in FY27 standalone business to help service debt
items.quote: In addition, we are expecting in the current year in standalone business, about INR150 crores of the government benefits. This is not linked to the projects or these are not subsidies. These are special benefits, which are good, which would be released by the government in the current year

items.statement: Backup options include equity raising if government receivables delayed
items.quote: backup options are always available about refinancing, backup option about raising of the equity, etc. Those are available

items.statement: Food division IPO not immediate; unlikely in first half of FY27, will reassess in second half
items.quote: I don't see that immediately happening, at least not in the first half. We will see how things change post some of these uncertainties go away in the second half

items.statement: Collaboration with Japanese company Kagome for tomato processing plant starting next tomato season
items.quote: The other business which we are working on a collaboration with the Japanese company, it's about tomato processing. That plant would start sometimes, I think, January. That is the next mango season -- sorry, tomato season when that comes through

items.statement: Working with Reliance Consumer and Kagome on beverage and tomato partnerships; also work with Coca-Cola, Nestle, Unilever
items.quote: We are definitely working with Reliance Consumer. They are also our customers, and we are doing more things with them. As we do also, for example, Coca-Cola has been our customers for 15, 20 years. We work with Nestle, Unilever, all different types of people, the global food companies, Indian companies

items.statement: Receivables improved to 11.5 crore from 17.3 crore year-on-year, debtor days reduced to 65-70 days from 90 days
items.quote: The receivables if I compare to previous financial year that is March '25, we were at 17.3 last year. This year we are at 11.5. So, there is an improvement in number of days vis-à-vis this year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was ₹79 crore in FY26, up from ₹26 crore in FY25.
items.quote: One of the most critical aspects I would want to bring to everybody's notice is that the total cash generated from operations during the past 12 months is a significant, robust number of ₹ 79 crore — up from ₹ 26 crores which was the cash generation from operations in the previous year.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance is about ₹94 crore as on date, versus roughly ₹50 crore last year.
items.quote: Our cash and bank as on date is about ₹ 94 crores versus roughly around ₹ 50 crores last year.

items.statement: Net cash on balance sheet increased by about ₹20 crore to ₹46 crore in FY26 from ₹26 crore in FY25.
items.quote: The net cash generated on the balance sheet last year was ₹ 26 crore. This year it is ₹ 46 crore. So during the last 12 months, we have added about ₹ 20 crores from where we were.

items.statement: Total cash and bank balance at end of FY26 was Rs 7.56 crore
items.quote: Total cash and bank balance at the end of the year, 7 crores 56.

items.statement: Receivable days expanded from 73 to 108 days; major portion is with related party and accelerated collection in April and May; currently maintaining 60 days DSO
items.quote: So usually, our timeline for the recovery of the payments is anytime between 30 to 45 days. So, major category falls under that. And the type of customers that we are dealing with are absolutely good level of customers, so we never face any kind of difficulty in the receivables.

items.statement: Receivable days expanded from 73 to 108 days; major portion is with related party and accelerated collection in April and May; currently maintaining 60 days DSO
items.quote: Yes. So, in account receivables, the major portion is with to the related party only, and that we have accelerated collection in the month of April and May itself. So, current situation like I will tell you that we are maintaining 60 days DSO on receivable side.

items.statement: Not planning equity dilution or rights issue this year; will use different funding arrangements for future acquisitions
items.quote: I don't think so. Not, not so early. Not this year at least.

items.statement: Consolidated cash as of 31st March was ₹1,362 million and net cash was ₹590 million after outstanding debt
items.quote: The consolidated cash as of 31st March was ₹1,362 million, and the net cash was ₹590 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased to INR 162 crores from INR 115 crores due to higher ad revenue and Dhurandhar release timing
items.quote: One of the key reasons for the increase is that advertisement sales typically have a realization cycle of anywhere between 110 to 150 or even 160 days, depending on whether the client belongs to the corporate or government segment.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO for current year stands at 147 days compared to 121 days in FY25
items.quote: To give you some perspective on DSOs, or Days Sales Outstanding, the consolidated DSO for the current year stands at 147 days, compared to 121 days in FY25, and this increase is largely attributable to the reasons I just mentioned.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year despite INR 11 crores tied up in working capital
items.quote: Our net cash has improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year, despite nearly INR 11 crores getting further tied up in working capital.

items.statement: Management highlighted working capital management through inventory optimization and assortment focus as a key driver of growth.
items.quote: as part of working capital management, the number one point was in terms of managin g our assortment. So last year, there was extensive work done in H1 in terms of our optimization of our inventory, which started with looking at our assortment design or assortment strategy and looking at optimizing our SKU mix with a focus on, (a) lowering inventory at an aggregate level, but more importantly, put

items.statement: Management stated the mandate is to achieve EBITDA breakeven first, after which recapitalization options including equity infusion will be evaluated.
items.quote: The mandate to the management team is to do an EBITDA turnaround. And therefore, we are focused in terms of ensuring that we breakeven at the EBITDA level. I'm sure the moment that happens, that is a strong signal to everyone. And at that point of time, we will look at how do we recapitalize.

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned negative in FY26 due to higher working capital from strategic advance payments to vendors and inventory build-up amid supply chain uncertainty.
items.quote: while the company delivered healthy revenue last year, our operating cash flow was impacted mainly due to higher working capital during the year.

name: Star Imaging And Path Lab Ltd

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved to INR23.4 crores in FY26 from negative INR2.6 crores in FY25
items.quote: Operating cash flow improved significantly to INR23.4 crores compared to the negative operating cash flow that we had in the last year, INR22.6 crores in FY25.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used to repay loans, improving current ratio to 2.39
items.quote: Finally, after the IPO process, the IPO amount that came in was used to repay loans, due to which the current ratio has also improved. It has been 2.39, wh ich reflects a strong equity position for us, which is very big for us right now

items.statement: CMD says 7,800 ton capacity addition requires roughly INR35 crores.
items.quote: No, 7,800 tons, we require roughly INR35 crores.

items.statement: CMD says next year (FY28) capex for 2,400 tons LFC will be around INR60 to INR70 crores.
items.quote: next year when we go for a bigger project, that is for 2,400 tons, that time we are looking at investment of say around INR60 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: CMD says FY27 capex will be funded by debt only; FY28 capex by combination of debt and equity.
items.quote: This year it will be by debt-only, and next year will be by debt and equity.
